title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb mince under a mashed potato crust
excerpt: Lamb mince cooked low and slow with onion, carrot, and lamb stock, topped with a thick layer of buttery mashed potato and baked until golden. Classic British comfort food.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie takes its name from the fact that shepherds tended sheep, so the dish is made with lamb. The version made with beef is cottage pie. The term first appeared in print in 1877, though the concept of topping a meat filling with mashed potato as a way of using up leftovers is older. The dish became popular in Britain in the 19th century as an economical way to use yesterday's roast lamb. Today it is most often made fresh with mince rather than leftovers.

recipeTools.notes: A 28 x 20 cm oven-proof dish for baking.

content.text: Cook the lamb filling long enough that most of the liquid has reduced to a glossy sauce: a wet filling will make the mashed potato soggy. The mash must be thick enough to hold its shape when spread. Rough the surface with a fork before baking to create peaks that will brown and crisp in the oven.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pan. Brown the lamb mince in two batches over high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion and carrot over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute. Return the lamb.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Season. Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the sauce is thick. Remove the herb sprigs and bay leaves.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season well.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spoon the lamb filling into a baking dish. Spread the mash evenly over the top and rough the surface with a fork. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
